about: Sites the as-data checker sees but does not count: a string literal that spells a content id but is not one. One entry per (file, literal) with a one-line reason; it covers every occurrence of that literal in that file. The checker lists these separately, and an entry whose site no longer exists is STALE and fails (tests/as-data-check.test.ts), so this list cannot rot. `verbs` are closed lists kept in code on purpose (an id scheme with its own parser, generator geometry, a row schema): each names its dispatch and its sunset, is listed apart and never counted, and a verb whose declaration is gone fails the run. `tunables` (2026-10-13, widened): every top-level numeric const (and the named-constant rule's objects) in src/ and origins/ (tests and fixtures excluded) is a site; a NEW one fails --gate. Each keeper is `exempt` (stays in code by design: a version stamp, a wire format, a mirror, a browser constant; a specific reason, no expiry) or `debt` (owed as a row of its module: an owner and a real sunset date; --gate goes red on a debt past its sunset and warns 14 days ahead). Debt owners are the lane that owns the directory, unreviewed: correct your own entries. An entry whose site is gone is STALE and fails, so delete it when you move the number.
